newsitem.title: UK: U.S. Treasuries gain in London, tone weak.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries gain in London, tone weak.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries picked up some gains following Friday's sharp sell-off, but the tone remains negative, traders said on Monday.
"Friday's trading pattern was extremely bearish, and we should expect some sell-off in New York just based on that," said one trader from a Japanese bank in London.
The 30-year bond was at 102-12 at 1015 GMT, to yield 6.444 percent, compared with 102-07 at the Tokyo close and 102-09 at Friday's New York settlement.
The corrective action took place in thin volume, the trader said.
"There has been no swap business going through, no big deals."
Treasuries dropped two points on Friday after stronger than expected July U.S. employment data were followed by a strong National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index for July.

"Even though Friday's sell-off was probably a bit exaggerated in terms of reaction to the data, the underlying picture in bond markets is not particularly favourable," said Adrian Schmidt, international economist at Chase in London.
"We have probably seen the majority of the move, but the long bond yield can go to 6.5 percent," he added.
June construction spending, due at 1400 GMT was expected to have little impact on the market, but the quarterly refunding later in the week may put further pressure on prices, traders said.
The U.S. Treasury will sell $16.0 billion of three-year notes on Tuesday, $12.0 billion in 10-year notes on Wednesday and $10.0 billion in 30-year bonds on Thursday.
The September T-bond future was at 115-00, up 6/32 in automated trade.
